newsitem.title: USA: O.J. Simpson says he owes $700,000 in taxes.
newsitem.headline: O.J. Simpson says he owes $700,000 in taxes.

text.p: Former American football star O.J. Simpson said on Friday he owed about $700,000 in back taxes and may need to rent, rather than buy his next home when his multi-million Brentwood estate was auctioned off next month to pay his debts.
Speaking to reporters before heading to a court hearing on his assets, Simpson said the Internal Revenue Service was auditing his tax returns but he said he did not believe he broke the law.
"We've been working with the (IRS) since I've been arrested," Simpson said. "I don't think I broke the law in any way."
Simpson also said he was looking for a new house in Los Angeles but would probably rent because he could not afford to buy a home.
"I can't buy," Simpson said. "It'll be tough to buy."

Simpson was acquitted of the June 12, 1994, murders of his ex-wife, Nicole Brown Simpson, and her friend, Ronald Goldman, by a criminal court jury in October 1995. But he was found liable for their deaths by a civil court jury this year and ordered to pay the families of the victims $33.5 million in damages.
The families of the victims are currently asking a court to determine the value of Simpson's assets so they can collect on the award.
Fred Goldman, the father of Ronald Goldman, said he would be pleased if the government prosecuted Simpson for tax evasion. "That would be terrific," Goldman said.
During the hearing, Simpson was asked repeatedly about his 1968 Heisman Trophy, which mysteriously disappeared a few months ago and then suddenly showed up at a lawyer's office on July 18.

Simpson said he only learned recently that his business associate Mike Gilbert had the trophy. Asked why he did not notice the Heisman was missing from a glass trophy case at his home, Simpson said: "I have pictures and things at my house that I don't go around and look at every day. I mean it's like wallpaper in the house."
The trophy, which could bring about $400,000 at auction, was awarded to Simpson in 1968 as the best college football player in the United States.
Simpson's Brentwood estate is scheduled to be auctioned off on July 14 with a minimum bid of $2.5 million, to help pay off creditors.
